iterations.hypothesis: Transient wrist-force loads, amplified by single-sample tare and sampling at different rates, cause false guarded stops and inaccurate hold regulation. Averaging every encoder-transformed 500 Hz force sample over 50 ms will provide a consistent signal for all mission force decisions.
iterations.diagnosis: Mission0 has two false POWER contacts and mission1 one false START contact: wrist force reaches approximately 3.1 N with the TCP still 7–10 mm short and conductive force exactly zero. planner.py stops on one raw 500 Hz F/T sample, tares from one sample, and feeds the hold controller at 100 Hz. This permits transient inertial loads and sampling effects to masquerade as contact. Successful presses also show excessive conductive peaks of 23–42 N. Insert uses an EMA but still tares from a single raw sample. All three plates satisfy the supplied frozen slot checks; the observed metric failures correspond to extra press attempts.
iterations.expected_effect: Target improvement from 1/3 to 3/3: mission0 attempts 5→3, mission1 4→3, mission2 remains 3. False stops short of the panel should disappear and conductive peaks should decrease with more reliable 3 N regulation. Insert remains seated in all cases, although its touchdown timing may change. The average introduces approximately 24 ms of force-response delay, so peak reduction must be verified.
iterations.test_plan: Run the three full missions through the harness. Confirm exactly three registered attempts per mission, QUICK RUNNING, all steps OK, and unchanged frozen slot/door/basket success. Inspect conductive peaks for reduced impact and ensure touchdown remains reliable. Persistent zero-conductive stops refute transient-force suppression as a sufficient fix; increased contact peaks or degraded insertion indicate unacceptable filtering delay. No Python or simulation was executed.

iterations.diagnosis: Insertion is sensitive to lateral alignment at the intended tines. Lean improves from 20.58° at −5 mm dock x error to 7.94° nominal and 3.38° at +5 mm. Both failures detect touchdown and have no wrong-tine or other contacts, so touchdown alone does not establish correct seating. The failed runs also displace the basket inward by about 13 mm. pipeline.py aims using the original in-hand estimate despite measured pick slip; the resulting alignment can load a tine before the rim seats on the floor.
